# XRService

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("XRService")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

Where the player is in a headset: the head and the two hands. A controller's buttons, triggers and sticks are not here: they are `Enum.KeyCode` values whose names begin with `XR`, bound to `InputAction`s beside a gamepad's, and a controller vibrates through `HapticService` with `Enum.UserInputType.XRLeft` or `XRRight`.

Poses are in the play space: meters from the floor where the player stood when the session began, y up. `Workspace.CurrentCamera` places the play space in the world: the camera's `CFrame` is the play space's origin, and the head moves the view from there. A game moves its player by moving the camera, never the head.

With no headset, `Enabled` is false and every pose is the identity: a game that plays both ways branches on `Enabled` once, where it places its camera. A script reads the poses of the tick it runs in; the picture is drawn from later ones, at the time each frame is shown.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | — | read-only | Whether a headset is drawing this game. False on the screen, on a server and in a headless run without `--xr=simulated`. |
| `Passthrough` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether the player's real room is seen through the headset behind what the game draws. The room shows wherever the game draws nothing, and the sky is not drawn. `Lighting.XRPassthroughOpacity` fades the game's world over it. Nothing on a headset whose runtime has no passthrough (`SupportsPassthrough`). |
| `PointerHand` | `Enum.XRHand` | `Enum.XRHand.Right` | read/write | Which hand points at interfaces in a headset. Its ray finds the panels the screens become and every `SurfaceGui` and `BillboardGui`, and its trigger, or a pinch of its fingers, is a click where the ray meets one. |
| `PointerLength` | `number` | `5` | read/write | How far the pointing hand reaches, in meters, and how long its beam is when it meets nothing. |
| `PointerVisible` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the pointing hand's ray is drawn: a short beam ending in a dot where it meets an interface. It points, and clicks, either way. |
| `SessionState` | `Enum.XRSessionState` | — | read-only | What the headset is doing with this game: `Focused` while the player plays, `Visible` while the headset's own menu is in front, and `None` with no headset. `SessionStateChanged` fires when it changes; a game pauses on anything but `Focused`. |
| `Space` | `Enum.XRSpace` | `Enum.XRSpace.Standing` | read/write | Where the poses are measured from: the floor (`Standing`) or the head where the session began (`Seated`). A game that is played sitting down sets `Seated` once, at the start. The picture uses the same space, so the camera stands for the floor when standing and for the player's eyes when seated. |

## Methods

### `GetHandCFrame(hand: Enum.XRHand): CFrame`

Where a hand holds its controller in the play space, and how it is turned. The identity with no headset, and while the hand is not tracked (`IsHandTracked`).

### `GetHandJoints(hand: Enum.XRHand): { CFrame }?`

Returns the 26 joints of a hand tracked as a hand, with no controller in it, in the play space, or nil. The order is OpenXR's: the palm, the wrist, then each finger from the thumb out, from its root to its tip. A hand tracked this way is also held at its palm (`GetHandCFrame`), and a pinch of its thumb and index finger is the `XRPinchLeft` or `XRPinchRight` key. `[xr] hands = false` in `project.toml` turns hands off.

### `GetHeadCFrame(): CFrame`

Where the head is in the play space, and how it is turned: between the eyes, looking down its -Z. The identity with no headset.

### `GetPlayAreaBounds(): vector?`

Returns the size of the play area the player set up on the floor, or nil where the headset knows none. The width is x and the depth is z, in meters, centered on the standing space's origin.

### `GetPointerRay(hand: Enum.XRHand): (vector?, vector?)`

Returns where a hand points from and the way it points, in the world, as a unit vector: the ray a game casts for its own pointing. Nil and nil while the hand is not tracked, and with no headset.

### `IsHandTracked(hand: Enum.XRHand): boolean`

Whether the headset knows where this hand is now: false when its controller is put down out of sight, or asleep.

### `Recenter()`

Makes where the head is now the play space's origin, facing where it faces. When `Space` is `Standing` the origin stays at the floor's height. The poses after it, and the picture, are measured from there. Nothing with no headset.

### `SimulateInput(keyCode: Enum.KeyCode, value: number)`

Holds one of the simulated headset's controls at `value` from the next frame: 1 for a button down and 0 up, a trigger from 0 to 1, a stick's axis from -1 to 1. The key code is one whose name begins with `XR`. Only with `--xr=simulated`; anywhere else it raises an error.

### `SimulatePose(pose: Enum.XRPose, cframe: CFrame)`

Puts the simulated headset's head or a hand where `cframe` says, from the next frame. The pose is in the play space. A test uses it to move the player's head and hands from a script. An index fingertip puts that hand down as a hand tracked with no controller, its finger pointing along `cframe`'s look vector. Only with `--xr=simulated`; anywhere else it raises an error.

### `SupportsPassthrough(): boolean`

Returns whether this headset can show the player's room behind the game (`Passthrough`). False with no headset.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `SessionStateChanged(state: Enum.XRSessionState)`

Fires when `SessionState` changes.

### `UserCFrameChanged(pose: Enum.XRPose, cframe: CFrame)`

Fires when the head or a hand moves, once a frame for each that moved, with where it is now in the play space.
